Independent Monitoring Authority for the Citizens Rights Agreements

principles.name: Selflessness
principles.def: Act solely in the public interest.

principles.name: Integrity
principles.def: Avoid obligations that could influence official duties.

principles.name: Objectivity
principles.def: Make choices on merit and evidence.

principles.name: Accountability
principles.def: Be accountable and submit to scrutiny.

principles.name: Openness
principles.def: Be as open as possible about decisions and actions.

principles.name: Leadership
principles.def: Promote and support these principles by example.

LGA.name: Local Government Association: Model Councillor Code of Conduct

selflessness.evidence: Holders of public office should act solely in terms of the public interest.

integrity.evidence: Should not place themselves under any financial or other obligation to outside individuals or organisations that might seek to influence them.

accountability.evidence: Accountable for their decisions and actions to the public and must submit themselves to whatever scrutiny is appropriate.

openness.evidence: Should be as open as possible about all the decisions and actions that they take.

honesty.evidence: A duty to declare any private interests relating to their public duties.

leadership.evidence: Should promote and support these principles by leadership and example (Seven Principles appendix).

coc.doc_type: LGA Model Councillor Code of Conduct
coc.note: Local councils adopt the LGA model code, which sets out the Seven Principles of Public Life; individual councils' codes are not separately assessed.

LGA.basis: Every council must adopt a code of conduct consistent with the seven principles (Localism Act 2011, ss. 27–28). Most model theirs on this LGA code.

CO.name: Cabinet Office: Code of Conduct for Board Members of Public Bodies (2019)

selflessness.evidence: Holders of public office should act solely in terms of the public interest.

integrity.evidence: Holders of public office must avoid placing themselves under any obligation to people or organisations that might try inappropriately to influence them in their work.

objectivity.evidence: Holders of public office must act and take decisions impartially, fairly and on merit, using the best evidence and without discrimination or bias.

accountability.evidence: Holders of public office are accountable to the public for their decisions and actions and must submit themselves to the scrutiny necessary to ensure this.

openness.evidence: Holders of public office should act and take decisions in an open and transparent manner.

honesty.evidence: Holders of public office should be truthful.

leadership.evidence: Holders of public office should exhibit these principles in their own behaviour. They should actively promote and robustly support the principles and be willing to challenge poor behaviour wherever it occurs.

coc.doc_type: Code of Conduct for Board Members of Public Bodies
coc.note: Applies to the non-executive board members of central government bodies; section 3 sets out the Seven Principles. Individual bodies are not separately assessed.

CO.basis: Applies to all non-executive members on the boards of government departments, non-ministerial departments, executive agencies, NDPBs and national public corporations, and forms part of their terms of appointment.

WAL-LG.name: Wales: statutory code for council members

selflessness.evidence: Conduct of Members (Principles) (Wales) Order 2001, Schedule: members must act solely in the public interest.

integrity.evidence: 2001 Order Schedule: no financial or other obligation to outside persons that might influence them.

objectivity.evidence: 2001 Order Schedule: choices on merit in public business, appointments, contracts and rewards.

accountability.evidence: 2001 Order Schedule: accountable to the public and subject to appropriate scrutiny.

openness.evidence: 2001 Order Schedule: as open as possible, giving reasons, restricting information only where the public interest demands.

honesty.evidence: 2001 Order Schedule: duty to declare private interests and resolve conflicts to protect the public interest.

leadership.evidence: 2001 Order Schedule: promote and support the principles by leadership and example.

coc.doc_type: Statutory principles (2001 Order) with model code (SI 2008/788, as amended 2016)
coc.note: Applies to members of Welsh county and county borough councils, community and town councils, fire and rescue authorities and national park authorities (2001 Order, art. 2). Individual councils’ adopted codes are not separately assessed.

WAL-LG.basis: Local Government Act 2000 s.51 requires Welsh authorities to adopt a members’ code; the 2001 Order sets the statutory principles, which include all seven Nolan principles.

honesty.evidence: 2021 Code, section 2: duty to act honestly and declare private interests.

leadership.evidence: 2021 Code, section 2: promote and support the principles by leadership and example.

coc.note: Nine Scottish principles (duty, selflessness, integrity, objectivity, accountability and stewardship, openness, honesty, leadership, respect) include all seven Nolan principles. Applies to councillors.

SCO-LG.basis: Issued under the Ethical Standards in Public Life etc. (Scotland) Act 2000; every council’s code is based on it.

NI-SCH.name: Northern Ireland: school governor guidance (2026)

selflessness.evidence: Governor Guide Appendix 2: act solely in terms of the public interest.

integrity.evidence: Governor Guide Appendix 2: avoid obligations to outside bodies that might influence.

objectivity.evidence: Governor Guide Appendix 2: choices on merit.

accountability.evidence: Governor Guide Appendix 2: accountable for decisions and actions; submit to scrutiny.

openness.evidence: Governor Guide Appendix 2: as open as possible, giving reasons.

honesty.evidence: Governor Guide Appendix 2: declare private interests, resolve conflicts.

leadership.evidence: Governor Guide Appendix 2: promote and support the principles by leadership and example.

coc.note: Paragraph 4.2: school governors are expected to act in accordance with the 7 Principles of Public Life; Appendix 2 names and defines each. Applies to governors of grant-aided schools of every management type; unfunded independent schools excluded. National guidance, not proof each school has adopted a code.

NI-SCH.basis: Department of Education (NI) governor guidance; NIAO school governance guide independently states every governor should act in accordance with the principles.

WAL-SCH.name: Wales: school governing-body duties (2000 regulations)

integrity.evidence: Regulation 3(3): the governing body shall act with integrity.

accountability.evidence: Regulation 3(4): prepared to explain decisions and actions to interested persons (conceptual; not named).

openness.evidence: Regulation 3(4): shall be open about decisions and actions (conceptual; not the named principle).

coc.doc_type: Statutory conduct duties for governing bodies (Terms of Reference Regulations)
coc.note: Applies to community, foundation and voluntary schools (incl. community and foundation special schools and temporary governing bodies). Three principles are named; openness and accountability are required in substance; selflessness and leadership are not covered. Independent schools excluded. The 2024 induction-training syllabus does not itself constitute an adopted code.

WAL-SCH.basis: Education (School Government) (Terms of Reference) (Wales) Regulations 2000 (SI 2000/3027), regs 2–3, plus the national governing-body guide (ch. 2).
